passages.title: Oppression and the midwives
passages.summary: A new king enslaves Israel. Shiphrah and Puah refuse his order to kill boys. The ruler fears a growing people. The midwives protect life against his command.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how reverence for God can require resistance to cruelty.

passages.title: Moses preserved and exiled
passages.summary: Moses's mother hides him. Pharaoh's daughter adopts him. He later kills an Egyptian and flees. Moses survives because several women protect him. He later kills a man and flees Egypt.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Moses 1 expands Moses's later encounter with God. Keep that account distinct from his childhood.

passages.title: The burning bush
passages.summary: God calls Moses at Horeb. Moses must confront Pharaoh and lead Israel out. God hears the people's suffering. Moses questions his ability to carry the task.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church manual reads Moses's call as preparation for prophetic service.

passages.title: Moses returns
passages.summary: God gives Moses signs. Aaron joins him. Zipporah acts during a dangerous encounter. Moses voices his limits. Shared service and action carry the mission forward.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how help from others can accompany an assignment from God.

passages.title: Pharaoh increases the burden
passages.summary: Moses and Aaron ask for release. Pharaoh withholds straw but demands the same brick count. The first appeal brings worse conditions. The people question Moses's promise of deliverance.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider the strain of trusting a promise when conditions first become worse.

passages.title: God renews the promise
passages.summary: God promises deliverance and covenant belonging. A family record identifies Moses and Aaron. Harsh work leaves the people too tired to hear hope. God still promises to free them.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: The covenant promise includes belonging to God. Consider hope without blaming those exhausted by suffering.

passages.title: Staff and river
passages.summary: Aaron's staff becomes a serpent. The Nile's water turns to blood. The struggle reaches Egypt's source of life. Pharaoh continues to refuse release.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider the effects of a ruler's refusal on the people under his power.

passages.title: Frogs, lice, and flies
passages.summary: Three plagues strike Egypt. Pharaoh promises relief and then changes his decision. Pharaoh promises freedom when the frogs trouble him. He changes his mind when relief comes.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider whether your promises remain firm when immediate pressure ends.

passages.title: Livestock, boils, and hail
passages.summary: Further plagues affect animals and people. Some Egyptians heed the warning about hail. Some Egyptians shelter their workers and animals before the hail. Pharaoh admits wrong but later refuses freedom.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how repentance differs from a statement made only to end pain.

passages.title: Locusts and darkness
passages.summary: Pharaoh rejects full release. Locusts consume crops. Darkness covers Egypt. Partial offers keep the people under Pharaoh's control. The dispute concerns genuine freedom to worship.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how worship can require more than a restricted permission from a ruler.

passages.title: The final plague announced
passages.summary: Moses announces the death of the firstborn. Pharaoh still refuses release. The warning brings the conflict to a terrible cost. The account includes suffering beyond the ruler.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: How do the deaths in this chapter affect your understanding of Israel's freedom?

passages.title: Passover and departure
passages.summary: Israel keeps Passover. The firstborn die. Pharaoh releases the people. They leave Rameses. The meal becomes a lasting act of memory. Deliverance also carries grief through Egypt.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church manual connects the Passover lamb with Jesus Christ. Study the sign and the remembered deliverance.

passages.title: Remembering and the pillars
passages.summary: God commands remembrance of the firstborn and unleavened bread. Cloud and fire lead the people. Memory takes the form of household teaching. The chosen route avoids an immediate return through fear.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how repeated worship can teach children about God's deliverance.

passages.title: The sea crossing
passages.summary: Pharaoh pursues Israel. Moses stretches out his hand. Israel crosses and the army is overwhelmed. Israel fears the army behind them. The sea opens a path to freedom.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: First Nephi 17 recalls the sea crossing to teach trust in God.

passages.title: Songs and bitter water
passages.summary: Moses and Miriam lead songs. The people reach bitter water and then Elim. Praise and need follow each other. The journey still requires water after a great deliverance.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how gratitude and present needs can both appear in a life of faith.

passages.title: Manna and Sabbath
passages.summary: God provides manna and quail. The people gather food daily and rest on the Sabbath. The people must trust God for food each day. Gathering limits leave enough for others and allow rest.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church manual connects manna with reliance on God. Consider daily preparation and Sabbath rest.

passages.title: Water and Amalek
passages.summary: God provides water at Rephidim. Joshua leads the fight against Amalek while others support Moses. The people need both water and protection. Shared action supports leadership during danger.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider why support for others belongs alongside individual faith.

passages.title: Jethro's counsel
passages.summary: Jethro visits Moses. He advises shared responsibility for judging the people's disputes. One leader cannot carry every need alone. Delegation makes judgment more accessible.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how wise counsel can improve service and reduce an unfair burden.

passages.title: At Sinai
passages.summary: Israel reaches Sinai. God offers a covenant. The people prepare for God's presence. The covenant joins privilege with responsibility. Preparation marks the encounter as sacred.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church manual connects covenant belonging with duties of holiness and service.

passages.title: The Ten Commandments
passages.summary: God gives commands about worship and relationships. The people fear the encounter. Freedom receives a moral structure. The commands protect worship, life, family, and trust.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church manual studies how each command can shape faithful choices.

passages.title: Laws about servants and injury
passages.summary: The laws address servitude, violence, and responsibility for injury. These laws concern servants, injuries, and damaged property. People with different social standing receive different treatment.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider the difference between an ancient legal setting and present moral duties toward people.

passages.title: Property and vulnerable people
passages.summary: The laws address theft, damaged property, loans, and care for strangers, widows, and orphans. Justice concerns both property and people with little power. Israel must remember its own experience in Egypt.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: How can memories of need help you care for others?

passages.title: Justice, rest, and festivals
passages.summary: God commands honest judgment, rest, and annual feasts. An angel will lead Israel. Worship and justice belong together. The law includes care even toward an enemy's animal.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider whether your worship also changes your judgment and treatment of others.

passages.title: The covenant confirmed
passages.summary: Moses reads the covenant terms. Israel accepts them. Moses ascends the mountain. The people hear before they commit. A shared meal and sacred signs mark belonging.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: A covenant includes an informed promise. Consider the duties that follow your agreement with God.

passages.title: The ark, table, and lampstand
passages.summary: God gives plans for a sanctuary and its furnishings. The sanctuary centers on God's presence among the people. Material gifts support a sacred purpose.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church manual connects the tabernacle with worship and God's presence among His people.

passages.title: The tabernacle structure
passages.summary: God specifies curtains, frames, coverings, and the inner veil. The design marks distinct sacred spaces. Careful construction gives form to the worship setting.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how a prepared space can support reverence without replacing faithful conduct.

passages.title: Altar, court, and light
passages.summary: God gives plans for the altar, courtyard, and daily lamp oil. The outer space supports offerings and access. Continuing light requires repeated care.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider the repeated work that sustains a place of worship.

passages.title: The priests' clothing
passages.summary: God directs the making of Aaron's garments and the breastpiece bearing Israel's names. The priest wears the tribes' names before God. His clothing connects his service with the people.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider what it means to carry other people's needs within sacred service.

passages.title: Consecrating the priests
passages.summary: God gives instructions to appoint priests and make daily offerings. Aaron and his sons prepare for their duties through washing, clothing, and offerings.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church manual studies preparation for sacred service. Consider the duties beyond a title.

passages.title: Incense, washing, and sacred oil
passages.summary: God gives instructions for incense, washing, the census payment, and sacred oil. These repeated acts order worship and preparation. Sacred materials have a defined purpose.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how preparation can support worship without becoming only an outward routine.

passages.title: Skilled workers and Sabbath
passages.summary: God appoints Bezalel and Oholiab. The Sabbath remains a covenant sign. Moses receives tablets. Skilled workers help build the place of worship. They must also keep the day of rest.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how creative skill and Sabbath observance can both serve God.

passages.title: The golden calf
passages.summary: Aaron makes the calf. Moses intercedes, breaks the tablets, and confronts the camp. The people soon break their agreement with God. Moses asks for mercy, but many people die.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how quick substitutes for trust can damage a covenant relationship.

passages.title: Moses seeks God's presence
passages.summary: Moses meets with God outside the camp. He asks for guidance and God's continuing presence. Moses wants more than arrival in the promised land. He asks God to stay with the people.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider whether your requests seek God's companionship as well as a desired outcome.

passages.title: The covenant renewed
passages.summary: God declares mercy and justice. New tablets are given. Moses returns with a shining face. God renews the promise after Israel's failure. Moses brings the people instructions for faithful worship.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church manual reads renewal alongside repentance. Consider mercy with continuing responsibility.

passages.title: Gifts and willing work
passages.summary: Moses teaches Sabbath rest. The people bring materials. Skilled workers begin their tasks. The work uses willing gifts and different skills. Participation reaches beyond a single leader.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how willingness and varied skills can build a worshiping community.

passages.title: More than enough
passages.summary: The gifts exceed the need. The workers build the tabernacle's curtains, frames, and veil. Generosity serves a defined purpose. Leaders stop the collection when enough has been given.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how wise stewardship includes knowing when a collection has met its need.

passages.title: The furnishings made
passages.summary: Bezalel makes the ark, table, lampstand, and incense altar. The workers carry the earlier instructions into action. Repeated detail emphasizes faithful completion.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider the place of careful work in fulfilling a sacred responsibility.

passages.title: Altar, court, and accounts
passages.summary: The workers build the outer furnishings. The chapter records the materials used. Sacred work includes public accounting. The record names skilled workers and their responsibilities.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how clear records and accountable service can support trust.

passages.title: Garments and inspection
passages.summary: The workers finish the priests' clothing. Moses inspects the completed work and blesses them. Moses checks the completed work against God's instructions. He blesses the workers after the review.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how careful review can honor the work of those who serve.

passages.title: The tabernacle raised
passages.summary: Moses sets up the sanctuary. God's glory fills it. Cloud and fire guide later journeys. The book ends with God's presence among a traveling people. Deliverance leads toward worship and continuing guidance.
passages.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church manual connects the sanctuary with God's presence. Consider worship as part of the journey after deliverance.

events.summary: Moses and Miriam lead songs. The people reach bitter water and then Elim.
events.detail: Praise and need follow each other. The journey still requires water after a great deliverance.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how gratitude and present needs can both appear in a life of faith.

events.title: Manna and Sabbath
events.summary: God provides manna and quail. The people gather food daily and rest on the Sabbath.
events.detail: The people must trust God for food each day. Gathering limits leave enough for others and allow rest.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church manual connects manna with reliance on God. Consider daily preparation and Sabbath rest.

events.title: Water and Amalek
events.summary: God provides water at Rephidim. Joshua leads the fight against Amalek while others support Moses.
events.detail: The people need both water and protection. Shared action supports leadership during danger.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider why support for others belongs alongside individual faith.

events.title: Jethro's counsel
events.summary: Jethro visits Moses. He advises shared responsibility for judging the people's disputes.
events.detail: One leader cannot carry every need alone. Delegation makes judgment more accessible.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how wise counsel can improve service and reduce an unfair burden.

events.title: At Sinai
events.summary: Israel reaches Sinai. God offers a covenant. The people prepare for God's presence.
events.detail: The covenant joins privilege with responsibility. Preparation marks the encounter as sacred.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church manual connects covenant belonging with duties of holiness and service.

events.title: The Ten Commandments
events.summary: God gives commands about worship and relationships. The people fear the encounter.
events.detail: Freedom receives a moral structure. The commands protect worship, life, family, and trust.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church manual studies how each command can shape faithful choices.

events.title: Laws about servants and injury
events.summary: The laws address servitude, violence, and responsibility for injury.
events.detail: These laws concern servants, injuries, and damaged property. People with different social standing receive different treatment.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider the difference between an ancient legal setting and present moral duties toward people.

events.title: Property and vulnerable people
events.summary: The laws address theft, damaged property, loans, and care for strangers, widows, and orphans.
events.detail: Justice concerns both property and people with little power. Israel must remember its own experience in Egypt.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: How can memories of need help you care for others?

events.title: Justice, rest, and festivals
events.summary: God commands honest judgment, rest, and annual feasts. An angel will lead Israel.
events.detail: Worship and justice belong together. The law includes care even toward an enemy's animal.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider whether your worship also changes your judgment and treatment of others.

events.title: The covenant confirmed
events.summary: Moses reads the covenant terms. Israel accepts them. Moses ascends the mountain.
events.detail: The people hear before they commit. A shared meal and sacred signs mark belonging.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: A covenant includes an informed promise. Consider the duties that follow your agreement with God.

events.title: The ark, table, and lampstand
events.summary: God gives plans for a sanctuary and its furnishings.
events.detail: The sanctuary centers on God's presence among the people. Material gifts support a sacred purpose.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church manual connects the tabernacle with worship and God's presence among His people.

events.title: The tabernacle structure
events.summary: God specifies curtains, frames, coverings, and the inner veil.
events.detail: The design marks distinct sacred spaces. Careful construction gives form to the worship setting.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how a prepared space can support reverence without replacing faithful conduct.

events.title: Altar, court, and light
events.summary: God gives plans for the altar, courtyard, and daily lamp oil.
events.detail: The outer space supports offerings and access. Continuing light requires repeated care.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider the repeated work that sustains a place of worship.

events.title: The priests' clothing
events.summary: God directs the making of Aaron's garments and the breastpiece bearing Israel's names.
events.detail: The priest wears the tribes' names before God. His clothing connects his service with the people.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider what it means to carry other people's needs within sacred service.

events.title: Consecrating the priests
events.summary: God gives instructions to appoint priests and make daily offerings.
events.detail: Aaron and his sons prepare for their duties through washing, clothing, and offerings.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church manual studies preparation for sacred service. Consider the duties beyond a title.

events.title: Incense, washing, and sacred oil
events.summary: God gives instructions for incense, washing, the census payment, and sacred oil.
events.detail: These repeated acts order worship and preparation. Sacred materials have a defined purpose.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how preparation can support worship without becoming only an outward routine.

events.title: Skilled workers and Sabbath
events.summary: God appoints Bezalel and Oholiab. The Sabbath remains a covenant sign. Moses receives tablets.
events.detail: Skilled workers help build the place of worship. They must also keep the day of rest.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how creative skill and Sabbath observance can both serve God.

events.title: The golden calf
events.summary: Aaron makes the calf. Moses intercedes, breaks the tablets, and confronts the camp.
events.detail: The people soon break their agreement with God. Moses asks for mercy, but many people die.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how quick substitutes for trust can damage a covenant relationship.

events.title: Moses seeks God's presence
events.summary: Moses meets with God outside the camp. He asks for guidance and God's continuing presence.
events.detail: Moses wants more than arrival in the promised land. He asks God to stay with the people.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider whether your requests seek God's companionship as well as a desired outcome.

events.title: The covenant renewed
events.summary: God declares mercy and justice. New tablets are given. Moses returns with a shining face.
events.detail: God renews the promise after Israel's failure. Moses brings the people instructions for faithful worship.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church manual reads renewal alongside repentance. Consider mercy with continuing responsibility.

events.title: Gifts and willing work
events.summary: Moses teaches Sabbath rest. The people bring materials. Skilled workers begin their tasks.
events.detail: The work uses willing gifts and different skills. Participation reaches beyond a single leader.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how willingness and varied skills can build a worshiping community.

events.title: More than enough
events.summary: The gifts exceed the need. The workers build the tabernacle's curtains, frames, and veil.
events.detail: Generosity serves a defined purpose. Leaders stop the collection when enough has been given.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how wise stewardship includes knowing when a collection has met its need.

events.title: The furnishings made
events.summary: Bezalel makes the ark, table, lampstand, and incense altar.
events.detail: The workers carry the earlier instructions into action. Repeated detail emphasizes faithful completion.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider the place of careful work in fulfilling a sacred responsibility.

events.title: Altar, court, and accounts
events.summary: The workers build the outer furnishings. The chapter records the materials used.
events.detail: Sacred work includes public accounting. The record names skilled workers and their responsibilities.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how clear records and accountable service can support trust.

events.title: Garments and inspection
events.summary: The workers finish the priests' clothing. Moses inspects the completed work and blesses them.
events.detail: Moses checks the completed work against God's instructions. He blesses the workers after the review.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: Consider how careful review can honor the work of those who serve.

events.title: The tabernacle raised
events.summary: Moses sets up the sanctuary. God's glory fills it. Cloud and fire guide later journeys.
events.detail: The book ends with God's presence among a traveling people. Deliverance leads toward worship and continuing guidance.
events.uncertainty: Site markers follow a traditional regional reading. Many campsites and the sea crossing remain uncertain.

lds.text: The Church manual connects the sanctuary with God's presence. Consider worship as part of the journey after deliverance.

guides.title: Study Exodus
guides.description: Follow selected chapters through the book.

steps.title: Oppression and the midwives
steps.text: A new king enslaves Israel. Shiphrah and Puah refuse his order to kill boys. The ruler fears a growing people. The midwives protect life against his command.

steps.title: Laws about servants and injury
steps.text: The laws address servitude, violence, and responsibility for injury. These laws concern servants, injuries, and damaged property. People with different social standing receive different treatment.

steps.title: The tabernacle raised
steps.text: Moses sets up the sanctuary. God's glory fills it. Cloud and fire guide later journeys. The book ends with God's presence among a traveling people. Deliverance leads toward worship and continuing guidance.
